rationale: Drawer keeps context visible while giving enough room for detail or editing.
The ZIP reference defines the blurred overlay, side slide motion, rounded leading edge, footer, and scrollable body.
Drawer should not replace Dialog when the user must make a blocking decision.

items.rule: Dims the page while preserving enough context to understand origin.
Slides from a side with full-height surface, radius, border, and shadow.
Names the task and exposes close without hiding the object context.
Scrolls independent content without shifting the footer.
Pins primary and secondary actions to the panel, not the page.

items: Use role dialog with aria-modal true when the drawer overlays the page.
Move focus into the drawer and restore it to the trigger when closed.
Escape closes only when unsaved changes or destructive context are handled.
Keep header, body, and footer order predictable for keyboard and screen-reader users.
Use Dialog instead when a blocking confirmation is required.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines the panel purpose; state defines lifecycle, focus, and whether the trigger or panel is visible.

full-width.copy: Drawer uses the full viewport height while the panel keeps a defined width. The overlay is full-width; the surface is not.

demo.label: Closed drawer
demo.description: The user is back in the task.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Drawer stays side-aligned on roomy viewports and approaches full width on phones. Long bodies scroll while footer actions remain reachable.

viewport-organization.copy: Use Drawer when users need context plus room to act. Use Dialog for blocking confirmation and Menu for compact action lists.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for contextual detail, filters, or edits.
Keep page context visible when it helps orientation.
Pin footer actions for long content.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use Drawer for required destructive confirmation.
Do not turn it into a full route replacement.
Do not hide close or unsaved-change behavior.

groups.title: Review
items: Check focus restoration, Escape, overlay dismissal, body scroll, footer actions, and reduced motion.
Confirm phone width and action stacking.
Verify left and right motion direction.

mustTest: Role dialog and aria-modal when overlaying
rejectIf: The panel becomes a full route without navigation semantics.
Footer actions or close controls do not work.
Raw visual or motion values are used.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Drawer as contextual workspace expansion: agents can propose it for filters, detail, and edits while humans confirm if the moment should be a Dialog, Menu, or full route instead.
canDecide: Use Drawer for contextual detail or editing.
Use left side for filter/control panels when it matches layout origin.
Keep footer actions visible for long content.
mustAsk: The action is destructive or blocks progress.
The content may be a full page route instead of a panel.
rejectIf: Drawer contains a blocking destructive decision without Dialog review.
Close, Escape, focus, or scroll behavior is undefined.
The panel stretches or hides the page context without reason.
miel.handoff: I am using Drawer to keep context while expanding the workspace. Please confirm side, close rules, unsaved-change behavior, footer actions, and route escalation.
